newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares close slightly down in heavy volume.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares close slightly down in heavy volume.

text.p: Manila stocks paused for a brief respite on Tuesday closing slightly lower after a seven-day run-up as investors sold off blue-chip issues such as PLDT, traders said.

"We've gone through a profit-taking situation mostly on blue- chips. I think the market will be going through this sideways behavior until the U.S.market, which seems to be overbought, stabilises," said Harry Liu, president at Summit Securities.

"PLDT's rise the past few days was too much too soon and that could probably explain today's profit-taking. In the long term, we are very bullish about the market," said Helen Alvarez, research head at All Asia Securities.
Volume of shares traded reached 13.9 billion shares, amounting to 10.507 billion pesos, but most were block sales. Decliners trounced gainers at 63 to 49 with 77 issues unchanged.
Bogart Cruz, trading manager at Asia Pacific Capital Equities said that gainers trade were mostly thirdliners. He predicted that slight profit-taking in blue-chips may be sustained on Wednesday.
The market will test the 3,200 support level before pursuing the all time high of 3,375 points, Joey Roxas, president at Eagle Securities said.
